title: Corporate R&D Investments Following Competitors’ Voluntary Disclosures: Evidence from the Drug Development Process

scopes.description: The complete six-part supplied SAS preparation workflow, including the manual date-formatting stage, all required inputs, generated intermediates, and the Part 4 to Part 5 same-session WORK handoff. The separate Stata regressions are not supplied and are outside scope.

requirements.description: Part 1 requires the author-prepared ClinicalTrials.gov extract top50_concise.csv. It filters the author's interventional drug-trial/sponsor sample and uses trial type, intervention, phase, firm, results, funding, dates, NCT identifier, Conditions, and the Part 3 diagnostic field check. The file is absent; exact headers, sponsor selection, complete period, and the Excel date handoff are unverified. The supplied sponsor-identifier workbook is not the panel.

routes.description: The official page allows manual CSV field selection and the datasheet says the authors hand-collected a 2018 ClinicalTrials.gov extract. Neither verifies the author's sponsor list, historical snapshot, custom transformations, field names, `check`, or complete sample. Prefer the author-prepared CSV and specifications; do not replace it with a generic current download.
routes.expected_period: The source CSV coverage is unknown. Part 3 creates a 2005-2018 firm-market-year grid; Part 4 filters registration/start years to 2007-2017 and Start_dt to 01Sep2007-31Dec2017. These code bounds do not establish input coverage.

requirements.description: Part 2 requires the author-named MeSH_C_F_diseases.xlsx workbook to map normalized Conditions to disease and MeSH hierarchy values, producing mesh_class1/2/3. The workbook is absent; its year/version, matching rules, source columns, and disease/market coverage are unknown. Current NLM public product formats do not establish a compatible author-specific workbook.

routes.description: NLM documents MeSH products and free access, but not this author-created disease-to-hierarchy spreadsheet, its exact fields, or the edition/coverage used by the join.
routes.expected_period: No edition or production year is stated for the workbook.

issues.description: The required top50_concise.csv is not packaged. Its consumed headers, sponsor/sample selection, row coverage, date values, and author construction cannot be verified; the bounded one-row sponsor identifier workbook is not a trial-level panel.

Part 3 runs PROC FREQ on `check`, but the supplied program does not assign it. The CSV or generated Part 1 data may carry it through; presence is unknown, and it is not safe to invent a field or assume the diagnostic can be deleted.
MeSH_C_F_diseases.xlsx is not packaged. Exact author-named crosswalk edition, XLSX conversion, disease-to-mesh mapping, source field coverage, and join coverage remain unverified.

The source directs manual Excel short-date formatting and gives a month-year-to-15th rule, while Part 1 then parses text dates. No source workbook/range or saved/exported CSV handoff is supplied. Preserve the authored rule and do not infer a replacement conversion.

The SAS program uses one author-specific Windows folder macro for its library, inputs, and exports. That root is not the host workspace location; the root must be configured coherently before a future run.
Part 1 executes PROC CONTENTS on final3 before the DATA final3 step creates it. This diagnostic should be moved after its producer in a working copy; the rest of the program remains unchanged.

The supplied environment evidence leaves SAS startup unverified after TKELS failed to initialize. It does not prove a missing license or a successful runtime; no startup or author program is run in this assessment.

PROC EXPAND in Parts 3 and 5 requires the PROC EXPAND product component, identified by SAS documentation as SAS/ETS. Local product/version metadata are unavailable, so component availability is unverified.

The XLSX import and Stata file exports require the SAS/ACCESS PC Files interface under the documented SAS 9.4 product boundary. Local module availability is unverified; the CSV import alone does not require this interface.
The author-directed Excel date-preparation stage is part of the assessed workflow, but local Excel or compatible spreadsheet availability is not established.

The source uses DBMS=STATA for two .dta exports. An older official example uses STATA, while the SAS 9.4 reference names DTA; the intended local release is unverified. Do not treat the legacy spelling as a confirmed defect.

The archive supplies a datasheet, a 1062-line SAS workflow, and a bounded sponsor identifier workbook, but neither required input workbook/CSV is present. D0003-D0006 are generated by prior parts, and Part 4 WORK outputs feed Part 5 in one ordered SAS session; closure is therefore incomplete until inputs, manual handoff, and components are resolved.

evidence.description: The supplied datasheet title matches the frozen paper title apart from punctuation/layout; it provides no explicit DOI.
Part 1 counts sponsor trials, applies the author's greater-than-100 filter, and writes the generated trial-level D3 dataset.
PROC CONTENTS references final3 before the DATA final3 producer begins.

Part 1 derives start_yr and rgst_yr from parsed dates and completes the final3 data step.
Part 2 creates the generated trial-level dataset with MeSH classification, consumed by Part 3 and Part 4.
Part 3 imports the full input row into temp2 then runs PROC FREQ on check; no check assignment appears in this source block.
Part 3 expands the observed firm-market combinations to years 2005 through 2018.
Part 3 writes generated fmy_decile and exports a .dta file; this output is consumed by Part 6.
Part 4 filters MeSH markets and trial years/dates and constructs raw2 for later same-session use.
Part 4 creates WORK.myp0, saves myp_long and my_wide, and leaves mkt in WORK.
Part 5 defines two input-name macros but the shown code begins by consuming WORK.raw2 and does not use those macro names.
Part 5 joins Part 4's WORK.myp0, fy, and fmyp datasets; these require the same ordered SAS session.
Part 5 creates current-year measures, annual lag 1-2 variables, phase-2 leads 1-3, and market lags through PROC EXPAND.
Part 5 writes generated fmy_own123, consumed by Part 6.
Part 6 identifies fmy_decile and fmy_own123 as its inputs and derives two-period focal-firm lags.
Part 6 writes the final SAS dataset and .dta export for the later Stata regressions.

review_notes: The frozen title and DOI are retained. The datasheet title matches the frozen title apart from punctuation/layout; no DOI is stated in the supplied datasheet.

The target is all six supplied SAS preparation parts, not only the final script block. Part 4 produces WORK.raw2, WORK.myp0, and WORK.mkt for Part 5; preserve one ordered session and every named output. No Stata regression source is supplied.
The identifier XLSX is a sponsor lookup artifact, not the ClinicalTrials.gov trial-level panel. Its bounded sample is one header/row with coverage_verified=false; no values or entities are used here.

D0001 and D0002 are the missing input requirements; D0003-D0006 are generated by Parts 1, 2, 3, and 5. The exact frozen catalog name search found no ClinicalTrials.gov, MeSH, or trial-named local candidate; catalog metadata is not live-access evidence.

SAS startup remains unverified after the supplied TKELS initialization failure. PROC EXPAND requires SAS/ETS; XLSX import and Stata exports require SAS/ACCESS Interface to PC Files under the documented SAS 9.4 boundary. Local product/component metadata are unverified.

PROC CONTENTS on final3 precedes its producer and has a supported diagnostic-order repair proposal. `check` is called only by a diagnostic and its presence in the author CSV is unresolved. The SAS chained year/date comparisons are valid DATA-step range comparisons; no filter change is proposed.

DBMS=STATA appears in two DTA exports; older official SAS documentation uses that identifier, while the SAS 9.4 reference names DTA. Any rename is conditional on the verified target release, with both exports kept consistent.

Official product documentation checks were static only. ClinicalTrials.gov and NLM material does not establish the author input schema, sample history, MeSH workbook mapping, or compatibility.
